diagnostic_evidence.quote:
the roots of 
\[a_k(z)=\det(A_0^{(k)}+z A_1^{(k)}+z^2 A_2^{(k)})\] are 
\[\lambda_i^{2^k}, \quad \text{for} \quad k=1,\ldots,2m.\]

issues.failure_explanation: With the CR update as stated in (eq:crgen), the correct identities are A_0^{(k)} - A_1^{(k)}G^{2^k} + A_2^{(k)}G^{2^{k+1}} = 0 and R^{2^{k+1}}A_0^{(k)} - R^{2^k}A_1^{(k)} + A_2^{(k)} = 0 (similarly A_0 + \widehat{A}_1^{(k)}G - A_2^{(k)}G^{2^k+1} = 0 and A_2 + R\widehat{A}_1^{(k)} - R^{2^k+1}A_0^{(k)} = 0): the middle/last terms carry minus signs, not plus. Scalar counterexample: a_0=1, a_1=-5/2, a_2=1, g=1/2 gives a_0^{(1)}=-2/5, a_1^{(1)}=-17/10, a_2^{(1)}=-2/5, and a_0^{(1)}+a_1^{(1)}g^2+a_2^{(1)}g^4 = -17/20 \neq 0, while the minus-sign version vanishes identically. Likewise the roots of a_k(z) are -\lambda_i^{2^k}, not \lambda_i^{2^k}, and the exact recovery formulas for G and R have sign errors on the last terms. All downstream uses are sign-robust (the mis-signed terms vanish in the limits or enter only through bounds), so no conclusion is lost.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the signs of the four identities, of the two recovery formulas, and of the roots-of-a_k statement; no other change is needed because every downstream argument is unchanged (the mis-signed terms vanish in the limits or enter only via bounds).
issues.overall_effect: The four displayed CR identities, the exact recovery formulas for G and R, and the roots-of-a_k claim are false as written; the proofs that invoke them (the proof of prop:A0KW and the derivations of the subspace approximations in Section 4) contain false steps as written, though every conclusion survives with the corrected signs.
issues.title: The four CR identities in the unlabelled display (eq:crqme) have wrong signs
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local sign correction to displayed identities; every substantive claim, rate, and guarantee is preserved and no new lemma or construction is needed. It is reported rather than treated as a pure typo because proofs in the paper invoke the erroneous identities as steps, but the fix is short and loses nothing.

issues.failure_explanation: The first hypothesis as quoted is not the correct condition for the block shift-and-deflate conclusion, and it fails for the paper's own application: take m=2, ell=1, G=R=diag(1/2,1), W=I, so A(z)=diag((1-z/2)(z-1/2),(1-z)(z-1)) satisfies all standing assumptions (roots 1/2,1,1,2 with mu_1=1 double); with S_1=2, U_1=(1,0), S_2=1/2 the left side of the quoted first condition equals (1/4,-1/2), not 0, yet direct computation shows the transform is quadratic with exactly the stated coefficients. Moreover the two quoted conditions together do not imply the conclusion: A_0=0, A_1=diag(-2,0), A_2=diag(1,0), U_1=(1,0), S_1=1, S_2=2, V_2=(0,1)^T satisfy both quoted conditions, but the transform equals diag((z^2-2z)/(1-z),0), which is not a polynomial. The correct hypothesis is the eigenvector condition U_1 R = S_1^{-1} U_1 (given the factorization A(z)=(I_m-zR)W(zI_m-G)), equivalently the algebraic condition U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2+S_1U_1A_2V_2S_2Y-U_1A_0V_2Y=0 given the second condition; the application satisfies it since T_{R,1}R=\Lambda_{R,1}T_{R,1} and GW_{G,1}=W_{G,1}\Lambda_{G,1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the first hypothesis correctly - e.g., as the eigenvector condition U_1R=S_1^{-1}U_1 (which Theorem th5 already assumes) together with the factorization, or equivalently as the algebraic condition above - and note that the application satisfies it; no downstream result requires repair.
issues.overall_effect: The quoted Theorem th3.2 is false as stated, and the deflation construction in Section 3 that invokes it ("By applying Theorem 3.2 with ...") is unjustified as written. Because the correct hypothesis holds in the application, all downstream formulas and results (the \widetilde{A}_i coefficients, the factorization, prop:added-1, prop:added-2, thm:added-1, prop:added-3, and the reduced QMEs) remain valid.
issues.title: Quoted block shift-and-deflate Theorem th3.2 has a false first hypothesis, not satisfied by the paper's own application
issues.why_classification: A quoted theorem is flatly false and the paper's application does not satisfy its stated hypothesis, so the justification chain has a genuine gap; repairing it requires re-deriving/restating the correct hypothesis (a contained but nontrivial correction), though no result is lost because the correct hypothesis holds in the application.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that CR can be carried out without a breakdown and that the sequences \eqref{eq:crgen} generated by CR are bounded.

From the  condition \eqref{eq:roots_separation}, as $k \rightarrow \infty$,  $a_k(z)$ has exactly $m-\ell$ zeros that converge to 0, which implies that $\lim_{k\to\infty}{\nullity(A_0^{(k)})}= m-\ell$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claim is false. Counterexample: m=2, ell=1, G=R=diag(1/2,1), W=I_2, so A(z)=diag((1-z/2)(z-1/2),(1-z)(z-1)) meets all standing assumptions (|lambda_1|=1/2<1=|mu_1|<|lambda_4|=2, mu_1=1 double) and CR runs without breakdown with all iterates bounded (A_0^{(k)} and A_2^{(k)} tend to 0, A_1^{(k)} converges), yet A_0^{(k)}=diag(c(1/2)^{2^k}(1+o(1)),-2^{-k}) has both diagonal entries nonzero for every k (the (2,2) entry is -2^{-k}, the (1,1) entry decays like (1/2)^{2^k} but never vanishes in exact arithmetic), so nullity(A_0^{(k)})=0 for all k and the limit is 0, not m-ell=1; similarly nullity(A_2^{(k)})=0. The intermediate claim limsup nullity(A_0^{(k)}) >= m-ell is equally false in this example. The inference from "a_k has m-ell zeros converging to 0" to the nullity statement is also invalid: the zeros of a_k are the generalized eigenvalues -\lambda_i^{2^k} of the matrix polynomial, not eigenvalues of A_0^{(k)}, and eigenvalues of A_0^{(k)} need not vanish exactly. What does hold - and what the SVD step actually needs - is a gap between the ell slowly decaying singular values and the m-ell doubly exponentially decaying ones.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact-nullity claim by a correct singular-value-gap statement (the m-ell smallest singular values of A_0^{(k)} and A_2^{(k)} decay doubly exponentially, while the remaining ell decay strictly slower) and re-derive the subspace approximation of the invariant subspaces from that gap; the main limsup claims need no repair.
issues.overall_effect: The "Moreover" sentence of prop:A0KW (and its intermediate limsup-nullity claim) is false, and the justification it provides for the SVD-based subspace splitting used in the convergence analysis and in alg:isg is invalid as written. The proposition's main limsup bounds are unaffected, and the singular-value-gap phenomenon the algorithm relies on does occur, but it requires a correct argument.
issues.title: The nullity claim in Proposition prop:A0KW is false
issues.why_classification: A false claim must be removed and replaced by a correct gap argument (a contained reargument); the main convergence bounds and the algorithm's practical basis survive, so the loss is limited.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the number $\ell$, $1\le\ell\le m$, of eigenvalues of modulus 1 of the sought solutions $G$ and $R$

issues.failure_explanation: The advertised spectrum of \Lambda_{R,1} is wrong: the set {1/\lambda_{m+\ell},...,1/\lambda_{2m}} contains m-\ell+1 values, but \Lambda_{R,1} is (m-\ell)x(m-\ell), and 1/\lambda_{m+\ell}=1/\mu_\ell has modulus 1, whereas the eigenvalues of R inside the open unit disk are {1/\lambda_{m+\ell+1},...,1/\lambda_{2m}} (m-\ell values, per the assumptions in Section 2.2); the formula actually computed for \Lambda_{R,1} has the latter spectrum. The input specification also allows ell=m (the standing assumption is 1<=ell<m, and for ell=m the matrix W_{G,1} would be empty), and the return formula for \Lambda_{R,1} uses (\widehat{A}_1^{(k)})^{-1} while the formula for \Lambda_{G,1} uses (\widehat{A}_1^{(k+1)})^{-1}, an inconsistent iteration index at the return step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the output specification to sigma(\Lambda_{R,1})={1/\lambda_{m+\ell+1},...,1/\lambda_{2m}}, restrict the input to 1<=ell<m, and use (\widehat{A}_1^{(k+1)})^{-1} in the formula for \Lambda_{R,1}.
issues.overall_effect: The input/output contract of alg:isg is misstated (wrong eigenvalue set and cardinality for \Lambda_{R,1}, overly broad range for ell, inconsistent iteration index); the computed matrices have the intended properties, so downstream computations (alg:gfull) are not corrupted, but the contract as written is wrong.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:isg misstates the output spectrum of Lambda_{R,1} (and the admissible range of ell)
issues.why_classification: Purely contractual corrections; the computation and all downstream guarantees are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Compute the generalized Schur decomposition 
$$Q^* M Z=T, \quad Q^* N Z=S$$
with $Q$ and $Z$ unitary and $T$ and $S$ upper triangular, and where all matrices are partitioned as block $2 \times 2$ matrices with $\ell \times \ell$ blocks.
then $X$ is a solution of \eqref{eq:qmeB} if and only if

issues.failure_explanation: (a) The QZ step does not specify how to select the deflating subspace: by lem:added-1 the solutions of the QME correspond to deflating subspaces of the pencil (M,N), whose eigenvalues are the roots of det B(z), namely mu_1,mu_1,...,mu_\ell,mu_\ell (each mu_i double). The desired \bar{G}_{11} corresponds to one specific ell-dimensional deflating subspace (one direction for each mu_i), but the generalized Schur decomposition returns 2\ell Schur vectors in no canonical order, so Z_{21}Z_{11}^{-1} is correct only if the first \ell columns of Z happen to span that subspace; otherwise Z_{11} may be singular or the formula yields a different solution of the QME. Because the eigenvalues are multiple, extracting the correct deflating subspace requires additional work (e.g., Higham's selection procedure), which the algorithm omits; as stated it is not guaranteed to return the solution with eigenvalues mu_1,...,mu_\ell. (b) The alternative formula is incorrect: from MZ_1=NZ_1\bar{G}_{11} for the selected columns one obtains T_{11}=S_{11}\bar{G}_{11}, i.e., \bar{G}_{11}=S_{11}^{-1}T_{11}, not Q_{11}T_{11}S_{11}^{-1}Q_{11}^{-1} (the two differ for ell>1 because the blocks do not commute).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify a correct deflating-subspace selection (after the generalized Schur decomposition, extract for each mu_i the appropriate deflating direction as in Higham's method, or compute all solutions of the small QME and select the one with eigenvalues mu_1,...,mu_\ell), and replace the second formula by \bar{G}_{11}=S_{11}^{-1}T_{11}.
issues.overall_effect: alg:QZ, and hence the solve step of alg:gfull, is not guaranteed to deliver the stated solution \bar{G}_{11}; the incorrect alternative formula would in general compute a different matrix.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:QZ lacks a deflating-subspace selection rule and contains an incorrect alternative formula
issues.why_classification: The algorithm as stated can fail to produce the advertised output (a substantive gap in the procedure), and repairing it needs a nontrivial selection argument; however the QME is tiny (ell much smaller than m), so a contained fix avoids major loss.
